as_told.title: Chase Brandon, CIA Hollywood liaison, and his UFO book

plain: A former CIA man is said to have hidden real secrets about the 1947 Roswell crash inside a novel. Roswell is the town in New Mexico where many believe a craft from elsewhere came down. The man is Chase Brandon, who Michels says worked as the CIA's liaison to Hollywood. His book is The Cryptos Conundrum, published, as Michels has it, in 2012. Michels says Chase Brandon may be a pen name. Michels raises the book again and again. He says it deals with Roscoe Hillenkoetter, "one of the first CIA directors," and how he handled Roswell. Other times he stresses a secret committee on non-human intelligence, or a group called the Office of Strategic Assessment. He also says the book opens with a quote from the philosopher Francis Bacon: some truths are so strange they have to be hidden in fiction. Michels credits the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman as well. The other teller is a UFO researcher named Grant Cameron, who speaks without naming a source. He says the book was about how the CIA handled the Roswell crash, and that "according to some of the stories" the manuscript went through official review eight times. If true, it would mean the CIA let a true account out under cover of fiction.
